purpose: Imiglucerase is used to treat Gaucher disease, a rare inherited condition where the body cannot break down a certain fatty substance called glucocerebroside. This causes it to build up in organs like the spleen, liver, and bone marrow. This medicine helps reduce symptoms like an enlarged spleen or liver, bone pain, anemia, and low platelet counts.
how_it_works: People with Gaucher disease are missing or have very little of an enzyme called glucocerebrosidase, which the body needs to break down certain fats. Imiglucerase is a man-made version of that missing enzyme. When given through an IV, it goes into specific cells in the body and does the job the missing enzyme cannot, breaking down the fatty buildup and helping organs work better over time.
common_side_effects: Some people may experience mild reactions during or after the infusion, such as nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, flushing, itching, or mild rash. These reactions are usually temporary and manageable.
warnings: Some patients may have allergic reactions, including serious ones, during the infusion — tell your healthcare team right away if you feel chest tightness, difficulty breathing, swelling, or severe itching. Your doctor will monitor you closely during treatments. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should talk to their doctor, as use during pregnancy should be carefully considered. Always inform all of your healthcare providers that you are on this medication.
typical_dosing: Imiglucerase is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, usually every two weeks in a clinic or infusion center. The dose is based on your body weight and the severity of your disease, typically ranging from 2.5 to 60 units per kilogram per infusion. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you and may adjust it over time based on how you respond to treatment.
